description: DAVAR, New Caledonia's rural and food administration, runs the territory's agricultural statistics, and its monthly fruit and vegetable bulletin is the main short-term indicator of local food supply. Each month enumerators survey about 210 market gardeners and 340 orchardists on the quantities they sold and expect to harvest, and the four-page bulletin combines this with wholesale market price lists, price indices, import volumes, proposed import quota openings and a list of wholesaler-importers. The bulletin is used to regulate the market by opening imports when local supply falls short. The latest issue when read was No. 412 for August 2026, with an archive of earlier issues, and the statistics hub adds annual syntheses, an agricultural memento, a ten-year review and the agricultural census. All are free to download as PDFs. Caveats: publication was temporarily suspended when read, figures are in PDFs, not data files, the pages are in French, and no licence is stated. Coverage is the whole territory. Simulation uses: local production versus import shares for an island food system under cyclone or shipping disruption. Related records: the WFP global food prices database (data-wfp-global-food-prices) offers comparable price series for other Pacific states.
